title: Cryptocurrency Adoption in Entrepreneurial Companies Extending TOE to TxOEI
content: This study examines cryptocurrency adoption intention among entrepreneurial firms in Jordan and the role of individual entrepreneurial traits (IET). Using a sequential mixed-methods design, interviews with 30 entrepreneurs informed the development of the TxOEI framework, which extends the technology–organization–environment (TOE) framework by distinguishing macro technological conditions from micro cryptocurrency attributes and incorporating IET. Survey data from 390 founders and co-founders were then analyzed using structural equation modeling with bootstrapping. The qualitative findings highlighted transaction security, anti-crypto laundering, know-your-customer protocols, regulatory technology, and zero-knowledge proofs. The quantitative findings show positive associations between adoption intention and technological integration, security, infrastructure, traceability and provenance, fungibility and convertibility, resource availability, business innovativeness, customer willingness, religious acceptance, government support, risk tolerance, digital literacy, and competitive aggressiveness. Immutability and autonomy/decentralization did not have statistically significant relationships with adoption intention. Government support positively moderated the relationships of technological infrastructure and digital literacy with adoption intention, but its moderation of the resource availability relationship was not significant. The study provides an organizational perspective on cryptocurrency adoption in an emerging economy and demonstrates the value of considering founders’ traits alongside technological, organizational, and environmental conditions. The findings suggest that entrepreneurial firms should strengthen digital capabilities, assess transaction risks, and develop implementation capacity, while policymakers should provide clear regulatory guidance and address religious and cultural considerations. The cross-sectional survey design limits causal inference.
